messages:
maya: Flagging a regression seen in the japanese-vertical-ocr eval after bringing up nebula-q5-v2. Overall BLEU and WER moved in the wrong direction on the vertical+ruby subset. baseline fp16 WER=7.9% nebula-q5-v2 WER=15.8%
maya: Quick repro: raw OCR lines (vertical, ruby in parentheses) -> normalization -> detok -> model.generate. Same detok pipeline as other evals.
maya: Example raw OCR sample:
maya: ```
漢字(かんじ)
『漢字』
１２-３B
```
maya: Baseline output: "漢字かんじ 『漢字』 112-13B"
maya: Nebula-q5-v2 output: "漢 字 ( か ん じ ) 『 漢 字 』 １ ２ - ３ B"
hiro: That looks like tokenizer splitting at grapheme boundaries and losing fullwidth numeric grouping. Did you run tokenizer-only compare between the binary used in canary and the baseline runtime?
maya: yes. Baseline tokenizers wheel 0.13 yields: ["漢字","(","かんじ",")","『漢字』","\uff11\uff12-\uff13B"]
maya: Nebula-canary tokenizers wheel 0.14 yields: ["漢","字","(","か","ん","じ",")","\u300e","\u6f22","\u5b57","\u300f","\uff11","\uff12","-","\uff13","B"]
sasha: Interesting. Could be a pretokenizer normalization change (NFKC vs NFC) or a change in the pre-token-regex. Also check whether the build pulled a different unicodedata table (python wheel bump).
liam: Running a quick 1k-sample diff now, will post deltas.
eng-ml-bot: ci/tokenizer-compat-check queued for sha def456 (nebula-q5-v2)
noah: Can we confirm the container image manifest? sometimes onboarding images include an unpinned tokenizers or text-normalizer wheel.
eng-ml-bot: image-inspector: nebula-q5-v2-onboard image includes python:3.11, tokenizers==0.14.0 (unpinned), text-normalizer==1.2.3, s3-artifact: deadbeefcafed00d
hiro: If it's wheel mismatches, quick mitigation is to pin tokenizers and re-evaluate. Also add a smoke check in canary that runs a tiny vertical OCR sample to compare token counts.
maya: I pushed an override to pin tokenizers==0.13 in the canary image and kicked rerun.
canary-bot: Canary redeploy triggered for nebula-q5-v2-onboard (override tokenizers==0.13)
liam: Quick numbers: full 1k vertical subset WER delta before pin = +7.9% token-split-rate numeric/punct 2.5% -> 13.2%
liam: rerun with tokenizers pinned: WER back to +0.6% delta, token-split-rate ~2.8%
sasha: That strongly implicates the tokenizers wheel change. We'll treat weights as OK. Root cause: onboarding image floated a wheel bump.
hiro: Action items: 1) pin tokenizers in onboarding manifest and onboarding CI; 2) add tokenizer-version assertion in artifact metadata (model.tar contains tokenizers==...); 3) add a small unicode-normalization unit in the canary healthcheck; 4) inform infra to avoid floating python wheels in builder images.
maya: I'll open PRs for 1 & 3 and attach canary log snippets.
noah: Also propose adding a 'tokenizer-compat' label to model artifacts so the deployment pipeline can refuse mismatched runtime wheels.
liam: I'll write a short postmortem-blurb for PB/PMs explaining we misattributed a quantized kernel problem when it was preprocessing.
maya: thanks team, saved us from chasing int kernels. :slightly_smiling_face:
maya: i'll drop PR links here once CI passes.
